structuredIncident.summary: The R3 exit carrier beam fell from the yoke into the mill pit at approximately 1:03 PM on October 14, 2024 (Turn 2). The incident occurred during an outage configuration where work rolls and backup rolls had been removed. Evidence indicates that while hydraulic systems were isolated and bled, a raised top backup roll balance remained in place without independent mechanical restraint or verification of its support condition after pressure removal. Video review suggests the beam was wedged against mill components before falling once relative movement cleared an interference point. Witness accounts describe visible rotation prior to impact but do not confirm crane involvement; operational logs contradict reports of active crane lifts during the event interval.
structuredIncident.focalEvent: R3 exit carrier beam falls from yoke into R3 mill pit
structuredIncident.actualImpact: Beam and link landed on sled and scaffold platform. No injuries reported as no team members were in the pit at the time.
structuredIncident.potentialImpact: Falling object hazard with potential for severe injury or fatality if personnel had been present below; damage to equipment (sled, scaffold) observed.
structuredIncident.normalState: During normal operation, carrier beam is supported by installed work and backup rolls. The yoke pocket retains the link assembly under load conditions defined by roll configuration.
structuredIncident.eventState: Work rolls removed; top and bottom backup rolls removed for outage scope. Top backup roll balance left isolated in raised position. B hydraulics shut off and bled. Carrier beam remained attached to link with keeper installed but appeared displaced relative to yoke centerline prior to fall.

timeline.description: Work rolls and top/bottom backup rolls removed for outage work.
Top backup roll balance left isolated in raised position; B hydraulics shut off and bled.
Hydraulic isolation valve reported to have slow bleed-through; cylinder fluid could move back through feed after shutdown.
Lockout verification record shows mechanical block ID field blank for gravity control.
Yoke moved downward gradually over approximately two hours; carrier beam remained wedged against mill spreader/posts.
Relative movement displaced carrier beam and link arm away from mill centerline.
Link-arm stop cleared cylinder lifting point or yoke.
Carrier beam fell from yoke into mill pit.
Beam landed on sled and scaffold platform; small window liner fell with it.

facts: Incident occurred at Indiana Harbor, R3 Roughing Mill Stand (Turn 2).
Beam fell intact; keeper and pin recovered on assembly.
No gross damage or fracture observed on beam, link, yoke pocket post-event.
Hydraulic system B was isolated and bled prior to event.
Top backup roll balance remained raised without documented independent mechanical restraint (block/crib).
Video shows gradual downward movement of the yoke over two hours preceding fall; beam did not move with yoke while wedged, then fell after link-arm stop cleared lifting point.
Witnesses observed lower end rotate and drop but saw no crane hook or person touching it.
unknowns: Exact mechanical clearance between raised balance assembly and mill spreader/posts under zero-hydraulic pressure conditions.
Whether the keeper alone was sufficient to retain the link against gravity once wedging ceased, given off-center displacement observed in video interpretation.
Specific verification method used (if any) for 'raised position' support after hydraulic isolation; record shows blank field for mechanical block ID.
Rate of fluid bleed-through or pressure decay on isolated branch without historian data.
Whether the handwritten turnover note regarding keeper inspection was acted upon and verified by a competent authority before Turn 2 work began.
Exact mechanical clearance between raised balance assembly and mill spreader under zero-hydraulic pressure conditions.
Whether keeper alone was sufficient to retain link against gravity once wedging ceased given observed displacement.
Specific verification method used for 'raised position' support after hydraulic isolation; record shows blank field for mechanical block ID.
Whether handwritten turnover note regarding keeper inspection was acted upon and verified before Turn 2 work began.
Was a rated mechanical block or independent support physically installed in the yoke pocket to hold the raised balance cylinder after hydraulic isolation?
What is the specific requirement in R3 Outage Procedure or JSHA regarding retaining a top backup roll balance when hydraulics are bled and work rolls are removed?
Does the Keeper design specification allow it to retain the link arm against gravity when the beam is off-center or displaced from the yoke centerline, as observed in video review?

Does the equipment manual or maintenance history define the top backup roll balance cylinder/piston design such that it relies on hydraulic pressure to maintain position, making mechanical wedging unreliable once fluid is bled?
Was the handwritten turnover note regarding keeper inspection acted upon and verified by a competent authority before Turn 2 work began, or was it merely noted without verification?
Was there a formal, signed verification record for the keeper installation prior to bleeding hydraulics? If not, why was reliance placed on an anonymous handwritten note?
Was there an engineering assessment establishing that 'wedging' provided a reliable barrier against gravity load? If not, why was this assumption accepted as sufficient?
Did a mechanical block physically exist on the gravity control point when hydraulics were isolated? If yes, why was it not recorded in the LOTO field?
Was there an engineering evaluation determining that the installed keeper could withstand the specific off-center loading conditions present during this event?
Operational log (R3-EV-010) contradicts the hearsay email and witness speculation regarding a crane bump; evidence supports rejection of crane involvement as cause.
The blank mechanical block ID field and the unverified nature of the anonymous note indicate that independent positive control was not documented or verified before Turn 2.

Operational log (R3-EV-010) shows no commanded crane travel or lift tickets for R3 bay during the event interval. Witness statement packet (R3-EV-09) explicitly states witnesses did not see a crane hook, rigging, or person touching it. The email rumor (R3-CH-003) is hearsay with unknown origin and time; logs contradict the claim.

Turnover log (R3-EV-006) notes a 'turnover note' regarding keeper check but does not confirm verification. Anonymous handwritten note (R3-CH-002) lacks author, time, or chain of custody; cannot be treated as authoritative evidence that the keeper was verified.
Re-run source adjudication in smaller batches before treating the evidence review as complete.
